_comment: Decided promotion candidates, and why. consumer-lint reports every page rule
that COULD be generic; this file records the ones already adjudicated so the
same question is not re-opened every release. A verdict is not permanent — it
names the condition that should reopen it.
Anything NOT listed here is an open question, and the weekly digest raises it.
Delete an entry to put its rule back on the agenda.

market-studio-composition.why: These compose SpicyCar's own first screen: a field-note cover index and exact-listing photo inserts sized around the existing decision evidence. The shared sc-dossier--studio recipe already owns the contained photo and corner-frame composition. These adapter pseudo-elements reserve this page's 28px caption and enlarged phone float while keeping its existing decision-height budget; another product need not use those dimensions or legacy markup. The cover, dossier, signal matrix, theme, and logo already belong to the shared system; its Decision brief demonstrates their reuse.
market-studio-composition.reopen_when: A second consumer needs the same compact exact-object photo insert or product-specific cover index layout.

dg-*.why: The SVG explainer vocabulary is genuinely generic — it knows nothing about cars — but it has one consumer, used once. A promoted family must be demonstrated and maintained in the style guide, which is a real cost against a family nobody else has asked for.
dg-*.reopen_when: A second project draws an explainer diagram.

to-top.why: Nothing here is page-specific: a fixed back-to-top control shown past two viewports of scroll, visibility-based so it leaves the tab order when hidden. Every long page wants it.
to-top.reopen_when: Queued for the next release that opens band 4c — carry it with the dense-surface touch targets.

flags.why: A flex row of chips is already expressible with the system's own layout utilities; promoting a named class for it would grow the sheet without teaching anyone anything new.
flags.reopen_when: The shape gains behaviour the utilities cannot express.

picks-title.why: This is the heading inside SpicyCar's own 'spicy picks' idea — the one block the rebuild deliberately kept local. Its name carries page identity even though its declarations do not.
picks-title.reopen_when: Never, while picks remain this app's own concept.
